AI customer service in China: an 11x market between 2019 and 2027

China is one of the markets where artificial intelligence applied to customer service is growing fastest. We covered the overall dynamics of Chinese AI in our article on AI in China. Here we focus on one specific segment: AI solutions dedicated to customer service.

According to data from LeadLeo, Frost & Sullivan and Eastmoney.com published by Statista, this market was worth 1.60 billion yuan in 2019. It would reach 18.13 billion yuan in 2027, more than an 11-fold increase. Amounts from 2023 onwards are estimates.

Fast growth, then an expected acceleration

The market first grew very strongly: 3.01 billion yuan in 2020, 4.87 billion in 2021, 6.68 billion in 2022. According to the estimates, it would reach 8.69 billion in 2023, 9.50 billion in 2024 and 10.25 billion in 2025.

Growth therefore slows between 2023 and 2025, before a new expected acceleration: an estimated 13.33 billion yuan in 2026, then 18.13 billion in 2027. The pace forecast for those last two years is the highest since 2021.

Keep in mind that all amounts here are in yuan, not dollars, and that values from 2023 to 2027 are estimates published by the sources, not observed data.

Even with this slowdown, the market would still grow by more than half between 2022 and 2025, according to the estimates.

The value is in software

The breakdown by segment is particularly telling. Software accounts for about 80% of the market throughout the period: 1.28 billion yuan out of 1.60 in 2019, 14.50 billion out of an estimated 18.13 in 2027. Hardware (0.13 then 1.45 billion) and support services (0.19 then 2.18 billion) remain small.

In other words, most of the value is not in contact center equipment, but in software that can understand, sort and analyze conversations with customers. That is where companies invest.

This goes beyond China: everywhere, what transforms customer service is not a new device, it is the ability to make use of what is being said.

What it means for European companies

The Chinese market is moving fast because it made customer service a priority use case for AI. Contact volumes there are huge, and companies quickly sought to handle them in an automated way.

For European companies, the lesson is not to copy that model but to keep its logic: AI applied to customer service creates most value when it helps understand customers, not just answer them. And it must do so within a suitable framework, especially regarding data protection.

It is also a reminder that competition between customer service software providers is global. European companies compare tools designed in China, the United States and Europe, and must factor in where their data will be processed.

The scale of the Chinese market also means that providers there will have large volumes of conversations to refine their products, which will raise the bar for everyone.

Understanding, not just answering

Customer service software covers two different functions. The first is answering: chatbots, automated replies, request routing. The second is understanding: analyzing what customers say to learn from it.

That second function is what automatic language analysis makes possible. It reads tickets, emails, reviews and call transcripts to identify recurring topics, emotions expressed and customers at risk of leaving. The models involved are Mistral, BERT, Llama, GPT or Claude depending on the case.

For a European company, it is essential that this analysis runs on data hosted in Europe. At custovox.ai, data is hosted in France and never used to train models.

Answering and understanding work best together: what customers say tells you which automated answers to improve.

The takeaway

A market growing 11-fold in eight years, 80% of it software: China shows where the value of AI in customer service lies. Companies that invest in understanding their customer conversations gain an edge that simple auto-reply tools do not provide.

To go further, our call centers page shows how this analysis applies to contact centers.

The figures are estimates and expressed in yuan, but the direction is clear and consistent with what is happening elsewhere: the money goes where understanding happens.

What this means for you

In China, 80% of the value of AI for customer service lies in software that understands conversations. custovox.ai brings that understanding to your tickets, reviews and calls, with data hosted in France.
